SUMMARY

AbbVie Inc.(ABBV+1.41%)reported third-quarter results that surpassed expectations, characterized by double-digit operational revenue growth and a subsequent increase to full-year 2026 financial guidance. Management reported that the immunology and neuroscience segments drove performance, helping to mitigate the ongoing revenue erosion of Humira and headwinds in the aesthetics dermal filler market. The company completed the acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics to deepen its immunology pipeline and announced a 5.2% increase in its quarterly cash dividend. The quarterly results included adjusted earnings per share of $3.82 and significant free cash flow generation that supports a 2.0x net leverage target over the next three years.

Operator:Good morning, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the AbbVie Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call.[Operator Instructions]Today's call is also being recorded. If you have any objections, you may disconnect at this time. I would now like to introduce Ms. Liz Shea, Senior Vice President, Investor Relations.

Elizabeth Shea:Good morning, and thanks for joining us. Also on the call with me today are Rob Michael, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Jeff Stewart, Executive Vice President, Chief Commercial Officer; Roopal Thakkar, Executive Vice President, Research and Development, Chief Scientific Officer; and Scott Reents, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer. Before we get started, I'll note that some statements we make today may be considered forward-looking statements based on our current expectations. AbbVie cautions that these forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in our forward-looking statements. Additional information about these risks and uncertainties is included in our SEC filings.

AbbVie undertakes no obligation to update these forward-looking statements, except as required by law. On today's conference call, non-GAAP financial measures will be used to help investors understand AbbVie's business performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are reconciled with comparable GAAP financial measures in our earnings release and regulatory filings from today, which can be found on our website. Following our prepared remarks, we'll take your questions. So with that, I'll turn the call over to Rob.

Robert Michael:Thank you, Liz. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. AbbVie continues to perform above our expectations, with another quarter of outstanding results. We are delivering top-tier sales and earnings growth and making significant progress advancing our pipeline. Given the strength of our business and our promising outlook, we are once again raising our full year guidance and increasing our quarterly dividend. Turning to our third quarter performance, we achieved adjusted earnings per share of $3.82, which is $0.07 above our guidance midpoint. Total net revenues were $17.4 billion, beating our expectations by $200 million and reflecting robust sales growth of more than 10%. This includes 9 key products that delivered double-digit growth.

Based on the strong performance across our business, including Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Vraylar, Ubrelvy, Qulipta and Venclexta, we are raising our full year revenue guidance by $200 million and have now raised total revenue by $800 million since the start of the year. Further underscoring our confidence in our long-term outlook, today, we announced a 5.2% increase in our quarterly cash dividend, beginning with the dividend payable in February 2027. Since inception, we have grown our quarterly dividend by more than 350%. Turning now to R&D. We are making excellent progress advancing our pipeline to help drive growth in the 2030s and beyond.

In immunology, we completed the acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, adding multiple differentiated assets in dermatology, respiratory and other related inflammatory diseases with significant sales potential. The lead asset, zumilokibart, will be starting Phase III development in atopic dermatitis later this year. Also in immunology, we received U.S. approval for Skyrizi subcu induction in Crohn's. This new dosing option demonstrated exceptional efficacy and further strengthens Skyrizi's robust growth outlook. We also continue to make substantial progress with our strategy to combine Skyrizi with complementary mechanisms to further elevate the standard of care for patients with IBD.

We have now started a large Phase IIb program in both Crohn's and UC with Skyrizi plus our alpha4beta7 382 as well as Skyrizi plus our TL1A 701. Moving to neuroscience. We recently expanded our Parkinson's portfolio with the FDA approval of Juvmo. Juvmo provides physicians and patients with a meaningful new treatment option and represents a sizable commercial opportunity for AbbVie. Along with Vyalev/Duopa, we expect our Parkinson's therapies to collectively deliver peak sales of more than $5 billion. We are also making excellent progress with our oncology pipeline. Etentamig in multiple myeloma has demonstrated very high efficacy as well as differentiated safety and convenience.

We have now submitted our application for etentamig in the U.S. and anticipate approval in 2027. In addition, we reported positive Phase III data for Epkinly in frontline DLBCL and expect regulatory submission next year. In summary, we are delivering strong execution across our business and see numerous opportunities to drive long-term growth. With that, I'll turn the call over to Jeff for additional comments on our commercial highlights. Jeff?

Jeffrey Stewart:Thank you, Rob. I'll start with the quarterly results for immunology, which delivered total revenues approaching $9.2 billion, reflecting operational sales growth of 16.6%. Skyrizi and Rinvoq continue to exceed our expectations, demonstrating robust growth across all indications. Skyrizi total sales were nearly $5.8 billion, up 22.9% on an operational basis. In psoriasis, Skyrizi prescription trends remain very strong. Recent oral competition is not having a substantive impact on our in-play patient share with Skyrizi continuing to capture roughly 1 out of every 2 new or switching psoriasis patients.

We believe that Skyrizi's best-in-class profile, which delivers 100% skin clearance for the majority of psoriasis patients, high durability of response, very convenient quarterly dosing, exceptional long-term safety and robust joint protection in psoriatic arthritis with strong data through 5 years of treatment sets a very high bar relative to other therapies on the market or in development for psoriasis. In IBD, Skyrizi is growing very robustly as well and continues to capture half of the new patient starts in the class. And we are very excited to be launching the subcutaneous induction dosing for Crohn's disease, which further strengthens our competitive position.

The data supporting this new delivery is striking, including impressive rates of endoscopic response and remission, particularly for CD patients in the frontline setting. This efficacy is clearly differentiated relative to our own Skyrizi IV formulation and will allow us to be very competitive versus all induction therapies available for Crohn's today. Our subcu induction regimen is delivered with the same on-body injector as our IBD maintenance dose, which has received very favorable feedback from gastroenterologists and patients both, including overall ease of use, dosing speed and comfort.

Now while access typically takes a couple of months to ramp, our commercial and medical teams have already hit the ground running, and we expect the subcu induction will accelerate our new patient share in Crohn's over the next several quarters. Overall, we remain very competitively positioned in gastro and psoriatic disease. We are raising our Skyrizi full year sales guidance for the third time this year, and we see a substantial opportunity for both market and share growth well into the next decade. Turning now to Rinvoq, which delivered global sales of $2.7 billion, reflecting operational growth of 24.3%.

Rinvoq is also exceeding our expectations with particularly strong momentum in both RA and IBD, where we continue to see growing in-play patient share. We are also excited for the indication expansion opportunities in dermatology with commercialization of Rinvoq for vitiligo and alopecia areata underway already in Europe and approvals expected for both diseases in the U.S. over the next several months. Recall these 2 new indications combined are expected to contribute nearly $2 billion of peak sales. Lastly, in immunology, Humira global sales were $683 million, down 30.6% on an operational basis, reflecting continued biosimilar competition. Moving to neuroscience, where we continue to outperform expectations across our leading portfolio.

Total revenues were nearly $3.4 billion, up 19.5% on an operational basis. In psychiatry, Vraylar global sales were nearly $1.1 billion, up 14.3%. Performance in both bipolar disorder and adjunctive MDD continues to be very strong, reflecting Vraylar's well-defined profile in terms of dosing flexibility, low sedation and the ability to treat a full spectrum of symptoms. In migraine, we continue to deliver robust sales growth driven by share gains and underlying market growth as well. Botox Therapeutic global revenues were approximately $1.1 billion, up 9.8%. Ubrelvy global sales were $449 million, up 26.9% and Qulipta global revenues were $398 million, up more than 38%. Menstrual migraine prevention represents another opportunity to further strengthen our leading CGRP profiles.

Recent positive data for Qulipta and forthcoming results for Ubrelvy in this new potential indication could support approval and commercialization in late 2027. We also have substantial momentum in Parkinson's disease. Vyalev total sales were $286 million, reflecting double-digit growth. We remain on track to exceed $1 billion in revenue this year. We are also launching Juvmo, another exciting new treatment for patients with Parkinson's. Juvmo selectively activates the D1/D5 dopamine receptors involved in motor control and can be prescribed now as both a monotherapy in Parkinson's as well as an add-on to standard of care.

And given Juvmo's distinct profile, including strong durable motor control and low rates of debilitating side effects such as impulse control disorder, somnolence and dyskinesia, it represents a sizable commercial opportunity. Sales for Juvmo are expected to ramp gradually over the next several quarters as we work to establish commercial and Medicare coverage, which is expected to be more broadly available starting in 2028. Turning now to oncology, where total revenues were $1.7 billion, up 0.9% on an operational basis. Venclexta is performing very well especially in CLL as combination use with BTK inhibitors is a preferred fixed duration treatment globally. Total sales were $803 million, up 10.7%.

Continued double-digit sales growth from Elahere here and Epkinly also helped to offset the expected revenue decline for Imbruvica, which was down 26.1% due to IRA pricing and competitive share pressure. I'm also very excited for our developing portfolio in hematology following positive data for both etentamig in multiple myeloma and Epkinly in frontline DLBCL. We anticipate their potential approvals will be an important catalyst for next year and immediately supported by our existing commercial resources, including a substantial heme sales force and medical affairs team. Lastly, in aesthetics, global sales were nearly $1.2 billion, down 1.8% on an operational basis. Botox Cosmetic total revenues were $669 million, up 4.1% operationally, reflecting improving market growth globally.

Juvéderm global sales were $222 million, down 11.8% operationally, reflecting continued headwinds in key dermal filler markets. While economic uncertainty and lower consumer confidence have pressured the aesthetics category over the last several quarters, we are starting to see signs of stability. And we think that bringing forward innovation like our new fast-acting short-duration toxin Boey represents a meaningful opportunity for more new patients to initiate an aesthetic treatment. The commercial rollout of Boey is now underway in Europe and Canada and patient satisfaction has been very high, particularly with the rapid onset, which is consistent with the data from our clinical program. So overall, I'm very pleased with the execution and the continued strong performance across our commercial portfolio.

And now I'll turn the call over to Roopal for comments on our R&D highlights. Roopal?

Roopal Thakkar:Thank you, Jeff. I'll begin with gastroenterology programs in immunology. We further strengthened our leadership position in inflammatory bowel disease with the FDA approval of Skyrizi subcutaneous induction in Crohn's disease, which was based on the Phase III AFFIRM study. Detailed results from this trial were presented at the recent ACG and UEG meetings, demonstrating exceptional results across all clinical and endoscopic measures. We are extremely pleased with Skyrizi's strong performance, particularly in patients who had not previously experienced advanced therapy. In this patient segment, unprecedented results were observed after just 16 weeks of therapy with 60% endoscopic response, 43% endoscopic remission and 74% for clinical remission.

These results highlight the potential of subcutaneous induction to further enhance Skyrizi's position in earlier lines of Crohn's disease. Additionally, the Skyrizi label was updated to provide health care providers greater discretion in determining whether tuberculosis evaluation is appropriate prior to treatment initiation, rather than requiring mandatory TB evaluation for all patients. Also at the UEG conference, results were presented from the Phase II TARGET-CD study, evaluating Skyrizi plus our novel anti-alpha4beta7 antibody, ABBV-382 in Crohn's disease. The combination resulted in a near doubling of endoscopic remission at week 24 compared to either monotherapy.

Additionally, gut gene expression data showed a clear improvement from active disease at baseline to early intestinal healing at week 12, followed by broader tissue restoration at week 24. Early changes reflected repair of the intestinal lining and restoration of the gut barrier, effects not observed with monotherapy. By week 24, these changes evolved into signatures associated with tissue repair, nerve recovery and normalization of metabolic function. We believe this progression from inflammation to healing and ultimately, tissue restoration may represent an important step towards modifying the underlying disease rather than simply controlling symptoms. These results support our strategy of combining Skyrizi with complementary mechanisms to achieve meaningfully higher levels of efficacy in IBD.

A large multi-arm Phase IIb trial is underway, evaluating Skyrizi plus 382 and Skyrizi plus 701, an extended half-life anti-TL1A antibody in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. In parallel, co-formulation work is ongoing in preparation for Phase III trials. Moving to dermatology. Positive top line results were recently announced from a Phase III study evaluating lutikizumab in hidradenitis suppurativa. At week 16, lutikizumab demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements across multiple measures of disease activity. HiSCR 75, which is a rigorous bar for defining clinical response was achieved by 31% of lutikizumab patients. Lutikizumab also significantly improved skin pain, disease flares and quality of life measures with improvement in pain reported as early as week 1.

HS remains one of the most underserved diseases in dermatology and these results support lutikizumab's potential to become an important new treatment option for patients with HS. Results from the 36-week blinded extension period will be available next year with regulatory submissions to follow in the second half of 2027. Based on these results, we plan to begin an HS platform study later this year to evaluate lutikizumab and in combination with our long-acting amylin analog, 295. Other mechanisms such as anti-TL1A antibody are also being considered. The Phase III program for Rinvoq in HS is also nearing completion, where we remain on track for 16-week top line results near the end of the year. Moving to atopic dermatitis.

Zumilokibart, Phase II results were presented at the EADV Congress, demonstrating rapid and meaningful skin clearance and itch relief. Phase III studies are on track to begin later this year. Turning to neuroscience, where in the third quarter, Juvmo was approved by the FDA for Parkinson's disease. Dopamine agonists have long been used to help manage symptoms and reduce reliance on oral levodopa escalation. However, currently available agents primarily target D2/D3 receptors and their use has been limited by adverse events. As a selective D1/D5 receptor agonist, Juvmo demonstrated strong motor control and a favorable tolerability profile with low rates of dyskinesia, sedation and impulse control disorder, which have historically impacted the use of dopamine agonists.

Additionally, long-term data continue to support a reduced reliance on oral levodopa when taking Juvmo. After more than 1.5 years on Juvmo, 93% of patients had not increased their levodopa dose and 94% of patients with early Parkinson's disease had not started oral levodopa. Physicians and patients now have a treatment option that targets dopamine pathways differently and may reduce the difficult trade-offs associated with D2/D3 agonist. In psychiatry, the emraclidine dose escalation study has completed. The 150-milligram dose will be utilized in the monotherapy and adjunctive Phase II studies in schizophrenia with enrollment expected to begin by the end of this year. This new dose is 5x the highest dose evaluated in the previous 2 pivotal trials.

The 150-milligram dose was well tolerated and no new safety signals were identified. We look forward to advancing this higher dose for schizophrenia, which may result in greater efficacy compared to prior studies. Doses have also been selected for the psychosis program, where Phase II studies in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease are expected to begin early next year. Moving to our psychedelic asset, bretisilocin, a Phase III trial evaluating a single-course acute treatment in major depressive disorder is expected to begin later this year. We also remain on track for additional Phase II data in monotherapy MDD by year-end, which will help inform the Phase II study evaluating repeat dosing for chronic use.

This MDD study as well as Phase II proof of concepts in post-traumatic stress, generalized anxiety and obsessive compulsive disorders are expected to begin in 2027. In migraine, positive top line results were announced from the Phase III LUNA study, which evaluated Qulipta for the preventive treatment of menstrual migraine. No medicines are currently approved for menstrual migraine attacks, which are considered more difficult to treat, more disabling, tend to last longer and have a higher tendency to recur. This underscores the need for effective treatment strategies for this distinct disorder.

In the LUNA trial, Qulipta demonstrated meaningful and statistically significant reductions in migraine days associated with the menstrual period meeting the primary and all 8 ranked secondary endpoints versus placebo. A regulatory application will be submitted soon in Europe. Additionally, Phase III results for Ubrelvy in menstrual migraine prevention are expected near the end of the year, which will potentially support a submission in the U.S. in early 2027. Moving to hematologic oncology. Positive top line results were announced from the Phase III CERVINO trial evaluating etentamig monotherapy versus standard of care in heavily pretreated triple-class exposed multiple myeloma patients.

Etentamig delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free survival and overall response rates with a manageable safety profile, supporting its potential to become an important new treatment option for multiple myeloma. BCMA-directed bispecifics and CAR-T therapies have transformed multiple myeloma treatment. However, their adoption, particularly among community-based centers remains limited by adverse events such as CRS, neurotoxicity and serious infections as well as the need for specialized monitoring with a differentiated safety profile, simplified onboarding and a more convenient once-monthly dosing schedule after a single step-up dose, etentamig has the potential to streamline treatment and expand access across settings, including community-based clinics. A regulatory application was recently submitted to the FDA with an approval decision anticipated next year.

Beyond the CERVINO program, 2 new Phase III trials were recently initiated for etentamig, one in combination with pomalidomide in second-line plus multiple myeloma and another as a monotherapy in patients with newly-diagnosed light chain amyloidosis. And at the upcoming ASH meeting, early results from a Phase II study evaluating etentamig plus daratumumab in frail, transplant ineligible frontline multiple myeloma will be presented with a third Phase III study potentially starting next year. Continuing with other hem/onc programs. Positive top line results were announced from the Phase III EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial evaluating Epkinly in combination with R-CHOP in frontline DLBCL. The study demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival compared to R-CHOP alone.

Epkinly plus R-CHOP showed an overwhelming treatment benefit at this interim analysis, reducing the risk of disease progression or death by 51% in a broad population covering patients with International Prognostic Index scores between 2 and 5. Importantly, this is the first Phase III study with a bispecific antibody combination to demonstrate a progression-free survival benefit in front line, supporting the potential for Epkinly plus R-CHOP to become a new standard of care in this setting, regulatory submissions are anticipated early next year. Turning to solid tumors. At the World Conference on Lung Cancer, results from a Phase I study evaluating our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, ABBV-1480 in frontline non-small cell lung cancer were presented.

These early data were particularly encouraging, given the activity observed in PD-L1 negative patients, a group which has traditionally been more difficult to treat. A Phase III study was recently initiated to evaluate 1480 in combination with chemotherapy in frontline squamous and non-squamous small cell lung cancer. We also intend to move quickly to evaluate 1480 in combination with our ADCs across several tumor types. Two Phase II studies evaluating 1480 plus Temab-A were recently initiated, one in non-small cell lung cancer and another in colorectal cancer. And a Phase II combination study with ABBV-706, our SEZ6 ADC will begin next year in small cell lung caner. Moving to obesity.

Detailed results were presented at EASD from a Phase I multiple ascending dose study evaluating ABBV-295 in adults with a mean BMI of less than 30. We continue to be encouraged by the emerging profile for this long-acting amylin analog. In the study, 295 demonstrated meaningful weight loss across multiple dosing regimens, a manageable tolerability profile and a PK profile that supports potentially differentiating dosing intervals of every other week or monthly. A Phase Ib study in obese patients is ongoing with interim data anticipated around the end of this year. Additionally, a Phase II trial in obese patients was recently initiated. Turning to aesthetics.

We continue to work closely with the FDA to resolve outstanding matters related to the complete response letter for Boey, resubmission to the FDA is anticipated before the end of this year, with a regulatory decision expected in mid-2027. Additionally, we are exploring a combination of Botox with Boey, which has the potential to deliver differentiated efficacy by combining the rapid onset of Boey with the durable effects of Botox. A Phase II study recently began to evaluate this combination in glabellar lines. In summary, we continue to make meaningful progress across all stages and therapeutic areas of our pipeline and look forward to several more important pipeline milestones during the remainder of this year and into 2027.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Scott.

Scott Reents:Thank you, Roopal. Starting with our third quarter results. We reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.82, which is $0.07 above our guidance midpoint. These results include an $0.11 unfavorable impact from acquired IPR&D expense. Total net revenues were $17.4 billion, reflecting robust operational growth of 10.5%, excluding a 0.2% unfavorable impact from foreign exchange. Adjusted gross margin was 85.1% of sales. Adjusted R&D expense was 13.9% of sales, and adjusted SG&A expense was 21.2% of sales. The adjusted operating margin was 48.7% of sales, which includes a 1.2% unfavorable impact from acquired IPR&D expense. Adjusted net interest expense was $688 million. The adjusted tax rate was 13.6%. Turning to our financial outlook.

We are raising our full year adjusted earnings per share guidance range by $0.11 at the midpoint to between $13.95 and $13.99. This guidance does not include acquired IPR&D expense that may be incurred beyond the third quarter. We now expect total net revenues of approximately $67.8 billion, an increase of $200 million. At current rates, we continue to expect a roughly 0.5% favorable impact from foreign exchange on full year sales growth. Our revenue forecast now includes the following approximate assumptions for several of our key products and therapeutic areas. For immunology, we are increasing our global sales outlook to $34.9 billion.

This assumes Skyrizi revenue of $21.8 billion and Rinvoq revenue of $10.3 billion, reflecting increases for both brands based on continued strong momentum. In neuroscience, we now anticipate global revenues of $13 billion, an increase of $300 million reflecting Vraylar sales of $4.2 billion, Botox Therapeutic sales of $4.2 billion and total oral CGRP sales of $3.1 billion. For oncology, we are raising our global sales guidance to $6.6 billion. This now contemplates higher Venclexta sales of $3.1 billion as well as lower Imbruvica sales of $2.1 billion. In aesthetics, our global sales outlook remains unchanged at $5 billion and now assumes higher Botox Cosmetic sales of $2.8 billion, offset by lower expected revenues across products and other aesthetics.

Moving to the P&L for 2026. We continue to forecast full year adjusted gross margin above 84% of sales, adjusted R&D expense of approximately $9.8 billion and adjusted SG&A expense of approximately $14.5 billion. We also anticipate an adjusted operating margin of approximately 46.7% of sales, which includes a roughly 1.8% unfavorable impact from acquired IPR&D expense incurred through the third quarter. Turning to the fourth quarter. We anticipate net revenues of approximately $18.4 billion, which includes a modestly unfavorable impact from foreign exchange. We also forecast adjusted earnings per share between $3.83 and $3.87. This guidance does not include acquired IPR&D expense that may be incurred in the quarter.

Finally, AbbVie's strong business performance continues to support our capital allocation priorities. Our cash balance at the end of September was $10.8 billion, and we generated approximately $14 billion of free cash flow in the first 9 months of the year, which includes nearly $2.7 billion of Skyrizi royalty payments. This robust free cash flow supports a strong and growing quarterly dividend, which we are increasing 5.2% to $1.82 per share beginning with the dividend payable in February of 2027, as well as capacity for additional business development where we continue to assess external innovation across all of our key growth areas.

Following the recent close of the Apogee transaction, we remain on track to achieve a net leverage ratio of 2x over the next 2 to 3 years. In closing, AbbVie has once again delivered outstanding top and bottom line results and our financial outlook remains very strong. With that, I'll turn the call back over to Liz.

Elizabeth Shea:Thanks, Scott. We will now open the call for questions. In the interest of hearing from as many analysts as possible over the remainder of the call, we ask that you please limit your questions to one or two. Operator, we'll take the first question, please.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]We'll go first to Vamil Divan with Guggenheim Securities.

Vamil Divan:Great. Thanks for all information on the call. Maybe if I could just as I know you're not giving formal guidance for next year yet, but if I could just ask about -- as we think about updating our models today, any sort of key pushes and pulls as we think about next year in terms of dynamics to keep in mind? And also just at this point, anything you can share around payer discussions -- Rinvoq and how we should think about...

Robert Michael:Thanks, Vamil. This is Rob. I'll take the first question, and Jeff will take the second question. So as we typically do, we'll provide 2027 guidance on the Q4 call, but we are certainly exiting this year in a very strong position. Our sales and earnings growth in 2026 will be the second highest relative to our peers. And we expect to deliver top-tier growth again next year. When I look at Skyrizi and Rinvoq, they're delivering incredible growth of $6 billion combined this year despite already being on the market for 8 years and with more competition.

If you think about where that growth is coming from, that $6 billion, $3 billion of it is in IBD across Rinvoq and Skyrizi with obviously a competitive entry in that space. $2 billion of that growth is in Skyrizi psoriatic with the competitive entry in that space as well. So we're seeing despite increased competition. Just tremendous growth from Skyrizi and Rinvoq. And we have several catalysts that will help drive their growth next year and beyond, including subcu induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's with higher efficacy and more convenient dosing that will give us an even stronger competitive position.

We'll see Skyrizi head-to-head data versus Entyvio, which will bolster our position in UC, and we will launch 2 new derm indications for Rinvoq, both vitiligo and alopecia areata. So we have very strong momentum in immunology to continue delivering robust growth next year and beyond. Then in neuroscience, we're on track to deliver growth of 20% this year. which has made us the industry leader. I expect the strong demand to continue for Vraylar, Ubrelvy, Qulipta and Vyalev, in addition to Botox Therapeutic, Juvmo, as was mentioned on the call today, and it's our new Parkinson's therapy.

That will also contribute to the growth, although the ramp will be more significant in '28 and beyond, given timing of Medicare coverage. And then I would also keep in mind that the IRA price for Vraylar will begin in 2027, so you should be modeling that in as well, although I'd say many of the sell-side models have appeared to have modeled that in. But clearly, I mean, we have a lot of momentum across our business to drive strong top-tier growth again next year.

Jeffrey Stewart:Yes, Vamil. It's Jeff. So we are beginning to close all of the arrangements with the large PBMs and payers. And I would say, overall, it's a very consistent story as prior years. Our portfolio of products will have very strong access and it's based on a lot of the demand and the profiles that we have. The physicians really like these products, they're leading products across almost all of our categories. And so we anticipate very good payer access. In terms of the immunology approach that low single-digit sort of rebate concession is something that I would continue to think about in your modeling.

Channels move around a bit, but that's typically been our pattern, and we continue to think that, that's a good level of guidance there in terms of as we move into '27 in terms of payer access. And I couldn't fully hear your question, but in terms of Rinvoq, very consistent answer, and we anticipate with the pending approvals of vitiligo and alopecia areata, as we move into '27 that those new indications will also be reflected with favorable access as we move into the new year.

Operator:We'll go next to Chris Schott with JPMorgan.

Christopher Schott:I just want to follow up on the full data from the Skyrizi subcu induction in Crohn's and that recent approval. Can you just help frame out the opportunity here? I guess, specifically, how are you thinking about market share dynamics going forward? And I guess, how quickly do you think that could play through as you think about just kind of the ramp of Skyrizi from here? And then my second question was on the pipeline and the role of Skyrizi and the alpha4beta7 in IBD. Just following the Phase II data, are you thinking of this as a drug that's for later lines of therapy or something that could be earlier in the treatment paradigm?

Just maybe kind of talk a bit more about how you're seeing that fit relative to Skyrizi and just other products being developed in the space.

Jeffrey Stewart:Yes, Chris. It's Jeff. I'll take the commercial stuff and maybe Roopal can give a quick flavor over the new data that was announced at ACG and UEGW. Yes.

Roopal Thakkar:So on the subcu data set, what you heard from us was very strong data. And when we compare it with our own Skyrizi IV induction, it's numerically higher and quite substantially higher in that treatment-naive setting, which is the current positioning of Skyrizi currently in Crohn's and UC. So it will further support that exact positioning. Because recall, with Rinvoq having a little bit of a label expansion that has allowed us for those patients that are deemed inappropriate for an anti-TNF, who can then use Rinvoq potentially right after Skyrizi. So that positioning, I should say, has been further substantially strengthened with this subcutaneous offering. So that's one point.

And maybe I'll touch on the alpha4beta7 combo and then go back to Jeff. So Chris, what we saw here was very strong efficacy in later lines, including patients who already used P19s, already used JAK inhibitors like Rinvoq. However, we also saw strong data in earlier lines. And we anticipate being able to see that in Crohn's and in particular, a lot of excitement from our thought leaders and how this combination can look in earlier lines of ulcerative colitis. Can we get much stronger disease control early in patients rather than waiting for a step-up in care, this can potentially modify the disease as I was describing based on gene expression.

Could you have much better outcomes in the longer-term reductions in hospital visits and surgeries. So as we move this forward, we'd be looking at early patients and in later lines of patients. And that's in Crohn's and UC. We would explore that with 382, which is the alpha4beta7 as well as with our TL1A antibody as well.

Jeffrey Stewart:Yes. And Chris, in terms of your commercial question, so we are excited about the recent subcu approval, and our field teams already are out there promoting this AFFIRM data that's now reflected in the U.S. label. So I think what's important, as Roopal said, these endoscopic endpoints are really resonating for several years now with the gastroenterologist. And that's the single largest market value driver of what preference is. And so when our experts and our IBD experts or gastros look at this affirm data, it's quite striking. So it's sort of very, very high rates, higher than our IV.

And when they look, of course, it's cross-study comparisons, when they look across not just IL-23 induction, but every single induction study that's been done to date, it really stands out. So as we've talked about over the last few quarters, the in-play share is roughly 50-50 in IBD versus the main competitor, we would anticipate certainly an acceleration in Crohn's where we have that approval.
